speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help me understand what's going on, could you describe the specific feeding difficulties you're seeing and how long you've noticed the abdominal distension? Also, has your son been having normal bowel movements, or is there any blood or mucus in his stool?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the stool contain blood or mucus, and has the baby passed any gas or had a bowel movement recently? I would also like to know if there is a family history of cystic fibrosis or if he has had recurrent respiratory infections.

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal sweat chloride test, cystic fibrosis is unlikely, so I suspect Hirschsprung disease. Has the baby passed meconium within the first 48 hours of life, and does he pass stool only after a digital rectal examination?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby did not seem to pass stool normally and the belly swelling has become more obvious. Feeding has clearly decreased over the past few days.

speaker: Doctor
text: I will perform a digital rectal exam to check for a tight anal sphincter and the "explosive" release of stool and gas. I also need to know if he has experienced any episodes of bilious vomiting.

speaker: Patient
text: The abdomen still looks swollen and the baby seems uncomfortable, especially in the lower abdomen.

speaker: Doctor
text: I will now perform the digital rectal exam to check for a tight sphincter and the explosive release of stool, which is characteristic of Hirschsprung disease. REQUEST TEST: Rectal_Biopsy
